subject: Renewal: VerticalScale — pricing guardrail & commit flexibility
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan@verticalscale.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — usage climb, price hold request

Markus / Monica,

Quick context: our Q2 usage has materially increased (attached Q1 export shows the trend) and the execs want predictability for the next 6 months while we finalize product changes that will shift traffic mid-year. We’re coming up on our renewal window (contract expires 2027-06-30) and have two asks from procurement: 

- A temporary price hold (6 months) to avoid step-up while we stabilize traffic patterns
- A modest commit increase (we’re willing to increase committed spend ~15%) but need some one-time credit to cover the recent overages during onboarding spikes

We’d like to see a couple of concrete options—one that preserves unit price for six months if we add capacity, and one that keeps the current commit but gives credits. Can you share a short proposal we can take to procurement next week?

Attaching: usage_report_Q1.csv

Thanks,
Jordan Ellis
Head of Platform Engineering
VerticalScale

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2027 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — usage climb, price hold request

Jordan — appreciate the context and the export. High level: we can structure three pragmatic paths depending on how VerticalScale wants to balance predictability vs. unit economics. I’ve attached a redlineable term sheet (VS_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf) and summarized options below. 

Option A — Scale & Hold (recommended if you plan steady growth)
- Commit +15% year-over-year (12-month term)
- Temporary 6-month price hold at current effective rate (no step-up)
- 8% committed discount on usage within committed units
- No one-time credit; faster onboarding support included

Option B — Conservative commit + credit (procurement-friendly)
- Keep current commit for next 6 months, then reassess
- One-time $50,000 credit to offset the recent onboarding overages (applies to invoice after renewal)
- 12% discount on committed units for 6 months
- 6-month price hold on tiers above committed allowance only

Option C — Tiered burst pool (flex-first)
- Add a burst pool (pay-as-you-go) with a capped per-token rate and a buffer credit to reduce volatility
- 5% discount for committed baseline; burst pricing managed via monthly true-up

We can also do a blended option: commit +10% with a $30k credit and a 6-month guardrail. If you want, I’ll prepare a one-pager for procurement comparing the three (cost projections included).

Next steps: which option should I formalize? If you pick A or blended, I’ll route to finance for pricing approval and to legal for a short amendment. If B, I’ll draft the credit addendum and proposed invoice schedule.

Attached: VS_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf

—Markus

Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: approval request — VerticalScale blended concession

Team — summary and ask: VerticalScale is pushing for predictability while they scale; procurement signaled they prefer a blended conservative offer. I propose we put forward the following as a commercial compromise so we close before their renewal date: 

Proposal (sales-approved, needs finance + legal sign-off)
- Term: 12 months (2027-07-01 to 2028-06-30)
- Commit increase: +15% over current committed units
- One-time credit: $50,000 applied across the first three invoices after renewal (distributed credit)
- Discount: 12% on committed units for first 6 months
- Price hold: 6-month guardrail that freezes the effective per-token tiers for committed and mid-tier burst band (applies to tiers up to 1.5x committed)
- Condition: if monthly usage >1.5x committed for two consecutive months during the hold, standard surge rates apply thereafter

Rationale:
- Protects the customer through product churn window (their ask)
- Preserves revenue by tying the hold to a moderate commit increase and a reasonable overage condition
- Credit-sized to resolve recent onboarding overages and remove procurement friction

Requested actions:
1) Monica — finance approval for the $50k credit and confirmation of billing schedule (can we distribute across three invoices?).
2) Marissa — legal to run a short amendment (I’ll attach a clean term sheet for redline). Need turnaround by Friday 2027-04-09 to make procurement cycles.

I’ve attached the working term sheet and projected P&L for the blended option. If we can sign this week, VerticalScale indicated they will commit to onboarding support and a rollout window that increases traffic predictability.

Thanks,
Markus
